memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"And the LORD said to Moses, 'Go to the people and consecrate them today and
tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes and be ready by the third day, because on
that day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.'"
- Ex 19:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three days of preparation before God comes down. Washing, setting apart, getting
ready.

We might wonder why. Does clean clothing make anyone fit to meet God? Obviously
not. No amount of washing bridges that gap.

But the washing was teaching them something. It was a physical lesson in a
spiritual reality: you do not simply wander into the presence of the holy God.
Something must change. Preparation is required.

Israel needed this. They had come from Egypt where gods were casual, local, and
manageable. The living God is not like that.

Notice, though, that God is the one who commands the preparation. He tells them
how to get ready to meet Him. Even the approach is His gift.

For Christians, the washing that actually matters has already been done. "He
saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit" (Titus
3:5). We do not prepare ourselves to become acceptable; we have been made
acceptable in Christ.

Yet there is still something here. Hebrews says we approach with confidence, and
also that we should draw near "with a sincere heart" (Heb 10:22). Confidence is
not casualness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has familiarity with God tipped over into casualness?
2. How do you prepare your heart before worship?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Christ has made me clean. Keep me from treating Your
presence casually. Amen.
